But we can assume we are in some directory. We need to navigate to temp directory. In typical Unix, temp directory is /tmp. But we don't have a tool to change directory. We can just list /tmp? But ls tool only lists current directory. There's no path argument. So we cannot list /tmp unless we are already there. We might need to use find? But find requires path. We can use find with path="/tmp". That will list all files under /tmp. But the user wants to list all files in that directory, including hidden. find will list recursively. But we can use find with path="/tmp" and name="."? Actually find returns all items. That might be okay. But they want to quickly browse them. We can list using find. Let's do find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will list all items recursively. But maybe we want just top-level. There's no tool for that. We could use ls but only current dir. We could use find with path="/tmp" and name=None, but that will list recursively. That might be acceptable. Alternatively, we could use cat? No.

We can use find. Let's call find with path="/tmp" and name=None.
